objective: Implement every pending Warrantor item and prove closure without conflating source presence, local verification, integration evidence, or production readiness.

status_definitions.open: No implementation closure evidence has been accepted.
status_definitions.in_progress: Implementation work exists but acceptance evidence is incomplete.
status_definitions.implemented_pending_ci: The change and local evidence exist; an independent CI run is still required.
status_definitions.verified_local: Acceptance passed in the local evidence environment; production or external integration proof may still be required.
status_definitions.blocked_external: Completion requires external infrastructure, credentials, hardware, publication, or independent review not present in this repository.
status_definitions.complete: Every stated acceptance condition has current retained evidence.

workstreams.title: Truthful deterministic gates
workstreams.note: Domain A authority-plane items shipped as reference implementations: A-7 act-scoped single-use capability tokens (closes the unscoped-bearer-token exposure); A-5 the warrant template library (versioned, signed, data-not-code, instantiated by narrowing); A-2 delegation-chain intersection (warrants delegate by subset, revocation voids the subtree); A-3 quorum warrants (t-of-n exercise, combined receipt); A-4 escrow/conditional warrants (activate on condition, sunset without operator action); A-9 policy analytics (conflict/dead-policy/blast-radius); A-11 the authority simulator (would-this-bind + minimal-delta, the differential oracle for C-9); A-6 authority algebra (the capability algebra as a test-vector-pinned spec — scope intersection, cross-plane composition, and the no-union-across-planes boundary, with a published conformance suite any third-party implementation is tested against); A-12 signed policy bundles (a distribution of policy as one digest-sealed, keyed-signature artifact that composes by overlay merge and fails verification on any tamper or duplicate id — the deployment unit A-1 emits and the notary loads). 14 + 14 + 16 + 11 + 11 + 11 + 10 + 14 + 14 tests green, clippy clean. Remaining Domain A: A-1 policy compiler (needs C-9 dataset + N2), A-10 real enforcement.

workstreams.title: P1-P12 normative protocols, bindings, vectors, and TCK
Integrated enforcement, evidence, data, and deployment plane
workstreams.note: Evidence + flywheel plane shipped as reference implementations: B-1 transparency-log (append-only Merkle log, third-party-verifiable inclusion+consistency, breaks the one-machine trust radius); B-2 time-anchoring (RFC 3161 TSA + countersigned custody behind one verify interface, externally bounded [t1,t2]); B-3 receipt-explorer (query layer that verifies every receipt shown, untrusted state for tampered/unsigned); B-4 cross-org-chains (transitive dependency verification across orgs, revoked citation breaks the chain); B-10 proof-of-erasure (destroy payload, retain digest commitment, attest erasure); B-11 receipt-stream (resumable-cursor filtered event stream, in-order no gaps/dupes); C-2 training-extractor (privacy-tiered, hold-out-leakage-controlled corpus intake); C-10 inference-router (local-first, policy-gated cloud escalation, fail-closed cap); C-1 promotion-pipeline (every stage receipted, deploy without a Promote gate receipt machine-refused); C-3 specialist-corpora (per-plane gated corpora, refusals recorded, no ungated model); C-5 model-security (extraction budget throttle + corpus source-pin poison detection); C-9 policy-pairs (simulator-validated NL→policy dataset, accuracy+equivalence gate); B-5 receipt-federation (peer-to-peer discovery/exchange/verify against a per-node issuer directory with no vendor fallback, privacy tiers — the protocol-not-product item and the 'what if the vendor disappears' answer); C-7 guard-graduation (measured recall bar, staged promotion a below-bar model physically cannot reach, guard as one of nine gates never sole authority); C-4 dataset-format (split-tagged records pinned by digest, structural hold-out leakage detection, provenance source-pins — the format that makes C-2's leakage control auditable from the file); C-8 eval-corpus (adversarial eval corpus with fail-closed scoring, coverage-gap detection, and a hard re-gate budget encoding the exhaustion lesson); B-7 deterministic-replay (re-execute a recorded run and prove byte-identical outputs and receipts, failing at the divergent step). 20+14+14+11+11+11+14+14+12+8+11+10+16+15+14+14+15 tests green, clippy clean. Remaining evidence plane: none code-buildable (B-7 shipped); remaining flywheel: C-6 console model (UI, not a pure reference crate).

workstreams.title: Supply chain, packaging, and verifiable releases
Tenancy, observability, resilience, compliance, and security assurance
workstreams.note: I-1 (build-catalogue Domain I, Wave 1) shipped as a reference implementation: root-of-trust deployment modes — self-custody default, t-of-n threshold signing, and escrow continuity — each with a key-ceremony drill and a root-compromise re-key playbook that keeps historical receipts verifiable with no trust gap, honoring the anti-goal against a centralized Warrantor signing root. H-1 (Domain H, Wave 2) shipped as the agent identity graph: a queryable, stranger-verifiable dossier (owner, operator, delegation ancestry, plane bindings, reputation events) assembled from signed records alone. I-8 (Domain I, Wave 3) shipped as the agent evaluation harness: a deterministic task/grader/pass-rate instrument with fail-closed missing-run handling and capability-tier assignment — the harness half of the model/objective/grader/harness/control separation, producing the numbers C-7/C-8 consume. H-2 (Domain H, Wave 3) shipped as agent-to-agent delegation contracts: the bilateral terms (scope, budget, deadline, revocation-notice window) riding on an A-2 warrant delegation, with a fail-closed state machine and settlement. H-6 (Domain H, Wave 3) shipped as the agent registry: versioned manifest discovery with highest-version lookup, per-version and whole-agent revocation, and publisher-trust filtering that fails closed. H-4 (Domain H, Wave 3) shipped as agent reputation: time-decayed (per-half-life integer halving), clamped aggregation of signed weighted events into a score and trust tier — the computation H-1 deliberately defers, so a stranger derives standing from the receipt record rather than from Warrantor's opinion. I-5 (Domain I, Wave 3) shipped as conformance-as-public-infrastructure: a versioned, digest-pinned test-vector suite plus an implementation-agnostic runner that fails closed on an empty suite or an erroring vector — the mechanism that makes 'open protocol, not product' verifiable (A-6's algebra suite is one instantiation). F-6 (Domain F, Wave 2) shipped as tenancy: a nested tenant→resource store where cross-tenant reads are structurally unrepresentable, with per-tenant quotas enforced fail-closed on write and a namespace digest for independent isolation checks — the partition K-2 invoices against. 14 + 11 + 14 + 16 + 14 + 14 + 14 + 14 tests green, clippy clean. Note on prior remaining items: I-7 key ceremony/rotation is already implemented inside I-1 root-of-trust (ceremony_drill/ceremony_passes/rekey/revoke) and is deliberately not duplicated as a separate crate; I-3 issuer directory is folded into B-5 receipt-federation's per-node IssuerDirectory (kept as architecture, not a mandated central directory, per the anti-goal). Remaining assurance work: observability (F-5) and resilience (F-3/F-7) are integration/ops concerns (telemetry wiring, chaos/failover harnesses) rather than pure-logic crates, and are deliberately not fabricated as half-implementations.

workstreams.title: Golden paths, completion audit, and release usability
Incident-class hardening (Domain M): transitive-egress invariant, zero-standing-secret handles, governed messaging, task-validity gate, third-party jurisdiction, and the eval-guard measured path
workstreams.note: Reference implementations with passing local tests (187 tests across the thirteen crates/modules; clippy clean). M1/R1: egress now enforces the transitive-egress invariant (check_closure) — the incident escaped through a chain of individually-permitted fetches, so the closure of induced destinations must stay sanctioned. M2/R2: credential-vault issues opaque, binding-checked, optionally single-use handles so an agent holds a capability token, never a raw secret. M4/R4: causal-verdict implements the phantom STRICT_CAUSAL scorer for real — an outcome is valid only if produced, consumed, and reached through a sanctioned, evidenced causal cone, so 'right flag, wrong route' and 'output discarded without being consumed' are violations. M5/R5: budget-governor is the graduated-tightening control loop the incident lacked — risk ratchets the leash down instantly and relaxes only one level per cool-down, with a fail-critical halt floor. M7/R7: swarm-detection reads the receipt graph for infrastructure coordination (credential pass-through, egress pivots, resource contention, message-board topology, beacon periodicity) and its severity bridges into the governor. M8/R8: revocation-verbs makes halting a pre-authorized, decision-rights-gated verb whose revocation propagates transitively across every dependent surface as a graph closure — the enumeration that took ten days of manual forensics, done in seconds. M9/R9: the conformance discipline is delivered by the existing containment-conformance suite (capability-elicited, anti-sandbagging, refuses fake PASS); the remaining work is a continuous red-team driver over the broader invariant set. M10/R10: harness-floor is the fail-closed pre-launch guardrail gate — no run below the floor, and capability-measurement runs that disable classifiers need a scoped approval, time-box, and enhanced containment (the 100× finding). M12/R12: incident-replay makes reconstruction a query (who/what/authority/path/evidence timeline) and exports Merkle-rooted, PII-redacted, verifiable evidence packs for external investigators — the routine version of METR's six-day, 1.2M-entry effort. AX-46 closed: eval-guard offers run_preflight_measured, which fails closed on any boundary it cannot observe. Production readiness and CI remain open per the status definitions.

workstreams.title: Monetization & business systems (build-catalogue Domain K): metering, licence boundary, funnel, design partners
workstreams.note: K-2 (build-catalogue Domain K, Wave 1) shipped as a reference implementation: the metering crate reads the receipt graph itself to produce tenant-scoped, digest-traceable invoices (per-receipt rates plus monthly platform fees by plan, integer micro-dollars), with verify_invoice as the dispute-resolution check — self-auditing billing as a trust feature; K-1 open-core-boundary (the BSL 1.1 boundary as a CI-checked licensing manifest — substrate stays Apache-2.0 forever by crate layout, product surface carries BSL-1.1 with a four-year change date, a wrong-family crate fails the build — so 'the open core will be reliclosed' is answered structurally). 14 + 11 tests green, clippy clean. Remaining Domain K: K-3 self-serve funnel, K-4 design-partner program, K-7 docs/academy (Wave 1); K-5 SI channel, K-6 co-sell, K-8 FTO posture (Wave 2).
